texts.preamble: Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora vs Mohit Arora on 19 November, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Virender Kumar Bansal Principal District & Sessions Judge North-West District: Rohini Courts: Delhi Cnr No. Dlnw01-002667-2024 Ca No. 64-24 Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora W/o Mohit Arora D/o Sh. Biharilal Kandhari R/o B-291, Malviya nagar, Jaipur, Rajasthan Versus Mohit Arora S/o Sh. Roop Chand Arora R/o H.No. 31, Indira Gandhi Nagar, Indore-452009 Date of institution : 19.03.2024 Arguments heard on : 04.10.2024 Date of pronouncement : 19.11.2024 Appearance: Ms. Meghna Malhotra, Adv. for the appellant. Sh. Yudhishter Sharma, Adv. for the respondent. Judgment
texts.facts: Present Appeal has been preferred u/s.29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred as PWDV Act) challenging the order dated 14.02.2024 whereby the trial court has directed Mohit Arora (hereinafter VIRENDER KUMAR referred as respondent) to pay Rs.5000/- per month to the BANSAL complainant Smt. Bindiya Kandhari (hereinafter referred as complainant/appellant) towards maintenance of the daughter by VIRENDER from the date of filing of the petition till she attains the majority 15:10:41 +0530 and has not awarded any maintenance so far as the complainant/appellant is concerned. 2. Out of the wedlock, one female child namely Kalindi Arora was born on 21.03.2002. The appellant has filed the petition under the provisions of PWDV Act. Ld. Trial Court has also failed to appreciate that the respondent is B.Com. Pass, doing business under the name & style of Kalindi, earning sufficiently and much better in comparison with the complainant, who is home maker and bearing the responsibility of maintaining and upbringing the daughter solely taking financial aid from the parents since separation.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the complainant/appellant submitted that the trial court has not exercised its judicial discretion judiciously resulting into miscarriage and failure of justice. The mother has to not only take care of the child and spend money on her upbringing but also has to spend substantial time and make efforts and, therefore, the quantum of maintenance should have been decided accordingly. 6. The daughter of the complainant/appellant is still pursuing her studies and is unable to maintain herself. The child has to be taken care till she is able to maintain herself and not on attaining the majority. 7. The daughter of the complainant/appellant has specific and essential financial needs, encompassing education, healthcare and basic necessities and it is the duty and responsibility of the respondent to fulfill the same. Ld. Counsel has also relied upon the judgment cited as Arun Vats v. Ms. Pallavi Sharma, 2020 (1) Crimes 133, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that: "7. Counsel has also relied upon the judgment cited as Vaibhav Singh v. Smt. Divyashika Singh, 2022 (3) HLR 504, wherein the Division Bench of Allahabad High Court has held that: Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora vs Mohit Arora on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55385217/ 3 Ld. Counsel has also relied upon the judgment cited as Kripa Narayan v. Mamta Pathak, 2016 (3) JCC 2026, where in it was held that: Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora vs Mohit Arora on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55385217/ 5 In our considered view, merely because the appellant-wife is a qualified post graduate, it would not be sufficient to hold that she is in a position to maintain herself. Insofar as her employment as a teacher in Jabalpur, nothing was placed on record before the Family Court or in the High Court to prove her employment and her earnings. In any event, merely because the wife was earning something, it would not be a ground to reject her claim for maintenance. Ld. Counsel has further relied upon the judgment cited as Manish Jain v. Akanksha Jain, (2017) 15 SCC 801, wherein it was held that: Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora vs Mohit Arora on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55385217/ 6 Ld. Trial Court has rightly not allowed any maintenance to the appellant and has also restricted the maintenance to the daughter on her attaining majority.

There are only three issues.

He is B.Com and not 10th pass and doing the business of garments and bedsheets but no such document has been placed on record.
On the other hand, the respondent has also not placed any document and alleged that he is only 10th pass and is not doing anything.

Therefore, to that extent, in my opinion, order of the Ld. Trial Court is required to be changed.
